cases.test_name: PCIe slot check ( x16 on slot 1 to 10)
cases.purpose: Verify that the populated PCIe slots 1 through 10 enumerate with the specified device identity and current x16 link width/speed in BIOS, UEFI shell, and the running OS, while separating read-only OS evidence from operator-only firmware views.
preconditions: The owner supplies the slot 1-10 topology, expected device/vendor identity per slot, population plan, allowed link speed, required x16 width, and whether empty or bifurcated slots are in scope; do not infer a missing-device result from a slot number alone.
A maintenance-safe console path is available for BIOS setup and UEFI shell observation, and the operator has the approved firmware navigation and exit procedure without changing settings.
Baseline BMC/host health, PCIe topology, power state, and timestamps are recorded; existing logs are preserved rather than cleared.
pre_check_commands: Collect read-only OS evidence with `lspci -Dnn` and `lspci -vvv`, including each target device BDF, LnkCap, LnkSta speed/width, AER/error state, and the current PCI sysfs topology; save timestamps and do not clear dmesg, journal, or SEL.
Record the expected slot/device map and compare OS BDFs to the owner-provided physical slot map; note firmware version, boot mode, and any populated slot that is intentionally absent.
safety_checks: Do not insert, remove, reseat, hot-plug, or power-cycle PCIe hardware as part of this readout; stop if the platform procedure requires physical handling or the management/host state is unstable.
Do not change BIOS/UEFI PCIe settings, link speed, bifurcation, or boot order merely to make a result pass; capture the current configuration and escalate discrepancies.
Treat a negotiated x16 width or speed as distinct from the device capability; do not accept output without matching the slot identity, expected device, and owner-approved specification.
required_packages: pciutils (`lspci`) for OS-side read-only evidence
Owner PCIe slot topology and speed/width specification
BIOS setup and UEFI shell access for operator verification
cases.test_command: PARTIAL: after user confirmation and an approved maintenance window, the agent may run read-only OS collection such as `lspci -Dnn` and `lspci -vvv` and parse LnkCap/LnkSta and PCIe error fields. A qualified operator must independently inspect the same populated slots in BIOS and UEFI shell with `pci`/`pci -i`, record the firmware views, and correlate all three views to the approved slot/device/specification map.
risk_notes: The agent can collect the OS view but cannot independently observe BIOS setup or UEFI shell output; a PASS based only on `lspci` would omit two required source phases.
The source does not provide the slot population, device identity, link-speed target, topology/bifurcation rules, or definition of how empty slots are evaluated.
PCIe hardware changes, firmware setting changes, or unapproved power cycles can damage hardware, interrupt the host, or change boot behavior; this review keeps the test read-only.
expected_evidence: Owner-approved slot 1-10 topology/population map, expected device identity, link speed/width, firmware version, boot mode, and handling of empty/bifurcated slots.
Timestamped BIOS, UEFI-shell `pci`/`pci -i`, and OS `lspci -Dnn`/`lspci -vvv` evidence matched to each target slot and device.
Per-slot comparison of negotiated LnkSta against the specification, capability versus current state, AER/error deltas, BMC/SEL, kernel/journal evidence, and final host/BMC health.
post_check_commands: After the operator confirms BIOS/UEFI collection, run or review the approved read-only OS commands and correlate BDF, device identity, slot map, LnkCap/LnkSta, and error fields; preserve the pre/post log delta.
Verify no firmware setting, PCIe population, power state, host availability, or management path changed during observation; escalate any mismatch instead of retrying with physical changes.
logs_to_collect: PCIe topology/specification and slot population map
BIOS setup and UEFI-shell `pci`/`pci -i` captures or operator checklist
OS `lspci -Dnn`, `lspci -vvv`, sysfs topology, AER/kernel/journal, BMC/SEL, and host health evidence
blocked_conditions: No approved slot/device/topology map, speed/width specification, access to BIOS/UEFI phases, or maintenance-safe operator procedure.
A target device is missing, mapped to the wrong slot, has an unexpected negotiated width/speed, or shows new PCIe/AER errors and the cause cannot be established read-only.
The host, BMC, power state, or management path becomes unstable, or physical/firmware changes would be required to continue.

safety_checks: Do not boot an installer, repartition, format, overwrite disks, enroll TPM keys, or alter secure boot without explicit approval and a dedicated target; the agent must not guess the disk or OS image.
Stop on wrong disk, installer prompt for TPM clear/ownership, encryption/key loss, boot/partition failure, storage error, firmware/security change, BMC/host loss, or inability to recover.
Do not use password-bearing SSH or generic `systemd-cryptenroll` as proof of installation/TPM support; preserve installer, kernel, TPM, security, and storage evidence without clearing logs.
required_packages: Owner-approved OS installer media/image/checksum and license
Dedicated target disk/drive, recovery media, and operator/KVM access
Read-only post-install TPM/OS/boot/storage/security tools
cases.test_command: BLOCKED until the owner supplies the OS/image, target disk, partition/encryption/security plan, TPM/secure-boot contract, operator approval, and recovery. After approval, a qualified operator performs the install; the agent may collect read-only post-install TPM device/version/capability, boot/security, storage, BMC/host, and installer evidence but must not initiate disk writes or TPM mutation itself.
risk_notes: OS installation is destructive to the target disk and may overwrite partitions, data, boot entries, encryption keys, or recovery; the source does not identify the image, disk, or data-protection boundary.
TPM enabled during installation can affect measured boot, disk encryption, key enrollment, and recovery; the source only says “can install OS” and gives no security criteria.
The reference post-install checks do not prove the install was safe or the correct TPM was used, and the source log-clear step would remove installer/storage/security evidence.
expected_evidence: Approved OS/image/checksum, target disk serial/partition plan, TPM/secure-boot/encryption policy, installer procedure, approval, and recovery.
Operator installation checklist/console records with disk identity, TPM-enabled BIOS state, installer result, boot mode, partition/encryption state, and timestamps.
Read-only post-install TPM devices/version/capabilities, kernel/boot/security/encryption, storage, BMC/host/network, installer logs, and final recovery/health.
post_check_commands: After the operator confirms installation and first boot, collect read-only TPM/OS/boot/security/encryption/storage/BMC/host evidence and compare with the owner contract; verify the correct disk and OS.

Verify no unauthorized TPM mutation, encryption/key loss, wrong partition, or boot/security change occurred, preserve installer/kernel/storage logs, and leave the dedicated target in the approved final state.
logs_to_collect: OS/image/checksum/target disk and TPM/secure-boot/encryption specification
Operator installer/KVM/disk/partition/TPM-enabled checklist and timestamps
Installer/kernel/TPM/boot/security/encryption/storage, BMC/host/network, recovery, and final health logs
blocked_conditions: Missing OS/image/checksum, target disk/data approval, TPM/security/encryption contract, dedicated target, operator/KVM, recovery path, or install criteria.
Wrong disk, data loss, installer/partition/storage/boot failure, TPM clear/ownership prompt, encryption/key issue, security change, BMC/host loss, or incomplete final state occurs.
Post-install TPM/OS evidence cannot be tied to the approved target or final storage/security/host state cannot be confirmed.

deepseek_original_review.ai_packages_needed: OS installer media (user provides) + tpm2-tools (post-OS check)
deepseek_original_review.ai_commands: -- TPM linux command (OS install with TPM enabled): verifying a clean OS install with TPM on is a long OS-install task the agent can stage (boot to installer) but needs the installer media + interaction; agent can verify the installed OS sees the TPM via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /dev/tpm0 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i tpm; systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-device list 2>&1" afterwards.
deepseek_original_review.ai_logs_output: return the post-install OS TPM detection (tpm0, dmesg, cryptenroll device list) so the user confirms TPM works with the installed OS.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek correctly marks this row PARTIAL because installation needs user media and interaction while post-install TPM readback can be collected, but the source lacks the OS image, target disk, data-loss boundary, partition/encryption/security policy, installer procedure, and recovery. GPT classifies it BLOCKED until those prerequisites are approved; no disk write, TPM mutation, or unsafe credential-bearing command is allowed and the source log-clear step is rejected.
cases.blast_radius: Target disk/data/partitions, OS/boot/security/encryption, TPM keys/state, firmware, BMC/host/network, recovery media, and installation evidence.
cases.recovery_procedure: Do not start without a dedicated target and recovery plan. If the wrong disk, data loss, installer/boot/storage/security/TPM failure, or key issue occurs, stop writes, preserve evidence, use the approved recovery media/procedure, verify disk/OS/security/TPM/host health, and escalate before retrying.
manual_steps: Owner supplies the OS/image/target disk, partition/security/TPM contract, installation approval, and recovery.
Qualified operator performs the install with KVM and records it; the agent collects read-only post-install evidence only after confirmation and end user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
cases.openhands_instruction: Do not install an OS, partition/format disks, enroll/clear TPM, alter secure boot, guess the target drive, or clear logs. Stop and request the approved image/checksum, dedicated disk, security/TPM plan, operator approval, and recovery path; collect read-only evidence after installation only. End user decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
